title: Carlos Chagas's birth chart
metaDescription: Carlos Chagas's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 17.2° Cancer. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Tightest of all, Venus holds a sextile to Mars at 0.0° — close enough to weld taste to drive. A sextile pays out only on effort; the scheme calls it opportunity rather than gift.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: 17.2° of Cancer is the Sun's exact seat — second decan, 10°–20°, sub-ruled by Mars in the old triplicity scheme. The degree is the address; the sign is only the street.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Cancer (23.2°), Venus in Gemini (10.4°), Mars in Leo (10.4°): thought steeped in tone and memory, attraction that begins as conversation, effort spent in bursts and openings.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Nothing in the geometry sits closer than Venus and Mars: 0.0° from an exact sextile. The scheme reads a sextile as a door left unlocked. Useful, and entirely dependent on someone walking through it. Behind it, Mars square Neptune at 0.9°, and Uranus square Pluto at 1.1° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: Mars opposes Jupiter while both square Neptune. A t-square aims the whole axis at its apex planet; the tradition reads it as the chart’s standing assignment.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The oldest layer of the scheme — seven planets, four conditions — flags two placements in this chart. The Moon in Scorpio at 17.1° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Saturn in Aries at 2.9° is in fall. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Balance, counted honestly across the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: elements water 3, fire 3, air 2, earth 2; modalities fixed 6, cardinal 3, mutable 1. Water weights a chart toward the felt and the remembered — information that arrives as atmosphere before it arrives as words. Jupiter was retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Scorpio for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.9° between midnight and midnight. Fast enough that its degree is approximate, slow enough that its sign is not in doubt. At the noon reference it stands at 17.1°.
